title: Add VPC control plane Terraform: multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, peering, security groups, Route53 integration
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds Terraform modules and installer hooks to provision multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 integration for the private control plane. Includes upgrade/rollback hooks and migration notes. Backwards-compatible when using default config; see docs for opt-in Route53 peering steps.
description: Motivation: customers deploying the private control plane across multiple AZs need repeatable Terraform that creates private subnets, interface endpoints for SSM/EC2/Route53 as needed, hardened security groups, cross-account VPC peering for control-plane-to-data-plane, and Route53 inbound/outbound peering records. This PR adds reusable Terraform modules consumed by the private-installer and implements upgrade/rollback hooks so existing clusters can migrate with minimal downtime. Checklist: - [x] Terraform modules for vpc-control-plane (multi-az subnets, route tables, NATs) - [x] Interface endpoint module and module wiring for SSM, EC2, ECR (where applicable) - [x] Security group templates for control-plane endpoints + least-privilege defaults - [x] VPC peering and Route53 zone peering support (optional via feature flag) - [x] Installer integration and Helm post-install hooks for migration/rollback - [x] E2E provisioning tests and terraform validate - [x] Docs + upgrade notes Changeset summary (high-level commits): 1) terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane: new multi-az subnet, route table, NAT gateway submodule + variables for AZ mapping 2) terraform/modules/interface-endpoints: create interface endpoints, endpoint policies, and security group attachments 3) terraform/modules/peering-route53: peering resource, route propagation, route53-inbound/outbound zones 4) private-installer: wire modules into installer pipeline, add flags for enable_route53_peering and peering_role_arn 5) helm/templates/upgrade-hooks.yaml: post-install/post-upgrade hooks to apply Terraform or roll back 6) scripts/upgrade_rollback.sh: idempotent apply/rollback helper used by hooks 7) test/e2e/vpc_provisioning_test.go: provisioning and cleanup e2e tests 8) docs/private-deployments/vpc-provisioning.md: usage and migration guide Files changed (high-level): - terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane/main.tf - terraform/modules/interface-endpoints/main.tf - terraform/modules/peering-route53/main.tf - private-installer/installer/terraform_integration.go - private-installer/helm/templates/upgrade-hooks.yaml - scripts/upgrade_rollback.sh - test/e2e/vpc_provisioning_test.go - docs/private-deployments/vpc-provisioning.md - examples/private/vpc-example.tf Review conversation (high-level): - Miguel Ortiz: "Can we make the Route53 peering opt-in by default? I'm worried about unintended DNS propagation for existing customers." Asha: "Yes — route53_peering_enabled defaults to false, documented in the variables and the installer flag. Updated docs call this out and include a migration checklist." - Priya Singh: "Please confirm the interface endpoints include endpoint policies restricting access to our control plane endpoints only." Asha: "Added endpoint_policy variable and default policy template that restricts to control-plane principals; tests updated." - Ethan Zhao: "E2E terraform apply is flaky in us-west-2; saw a race creating route tables in parallel." Asha: "Added a create_before_destroy ordering and a short backoff retry in the installer helper; re-ran e2e and it passed consistently." - Miguel Ortiz (approve): "Looks good, validated terraform and e2e locally. Approving to merge once CI green." CI summary: - ci/terraform-validate: pass - ci/tf-plan: pass - ci/e2e-provisioning: failed (flaky route table race) -> rerun -> pass - ci/lint: pass - ci/security-scan: pass Merge outcome: squash merged to main after approvals. Merge method: squash. Post-merge actions: - Automated deploy job kicked off to build a binary and publish new installer artifact. - Published docs site update and added migration guide to internal runbook. Migration notes: Existing single-AZ installs remain unchanged unless the operator enables multi-az migration flag. When enabling Route53 peering, operator MUST ensure cross-account peering IAM role (peering_role_arn) is configured; steps are in docs. Rollback guarantee: installer hooks will revert Terraform state and remove peering endpoints created during the failed migration to avoid dangling DNS records.
commits_summary: 8 commits: add vpc-control-plane module; add interface endpoints module; add peering/route53 module; wire into installer; add helm upgrade hooks; add rollback script; add e2e tests; add docs/usage and migration notes.
review_comments: Miguel Ortiz: request to default route53 peering to false (addressed); Priya Singh: request for endpoint policies (addressed); Ethan Zhao: reported e2e flake and asked for ordering fix (addressed). Approvals from Miguel and Priya before merge.
ci_checks: ci/terraform-validate: pass; ci/tf-plan: pass; ci/e2e-provisioning: failed->rerun->pass; ci/lint: pass; ci/security-scan: pass
merge_outcome: squash merged into main on 2024-11-15 after approvals and CI green. Release note drafted and docs published.
notes_for_ops: If enabling route53 peering for an existing cluster, follow docs/private-deployments/vpc-provisioning.md section 'Migration: Enable Route53 Peering' and ensure peering_role_arn is configured. Use the installer flag --enable-multi-az to trigger migration flow. For rollback, run scripts/upgrade_rollback.sh with the same release name to revert applied changes.
example_commands:
# preview terraform plan from installer
./private-installer/bin/installer apply --dry-run --release my-cluster --tf-dir examples/private -var 'enable_route53_peering=false'
# enable route53 peering after verification
./private-installer/bin/installer apply --release my-cluster --tf-dir examples/private -var 'enable_route53_peering=true'
